questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Seed Science
questions.question: In a maize grain, the single shield-shaped cotyledon is called the:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) scutellum
Why: The single cotyledon of grasses such as maize and wheat is the scutellum, which absorbs food from the endosperm.
Why not the others:
(B) The coleoptile is a sheath over the plumule.
(C) The aleurone layer is the protein-rich outer layer of the endosperm.
(D) The plumule is the embryonic shoot.
Key point: In cereals, the cotyledon is the scutellum.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Biochemistry
questions.question:
Match List-I (Vitamin) with List-II (Deficiency disease).

List-I
(A) Vitamin A
(B) Vitamin D
(C) Vitamin C
(D) Vitamin B₁ (thiamine)

List-II
(I) Beriberi
(II) Rickets
(III) Night blindness
(IV) Scurvy
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(III), (B)-(II), (C)-(IV), (D)-(I)
Why: Lack of vitamin A causes night blindness (III). Lack of vitamin D causes rickets (II). Lack of vitamin C causes scurvy (IV). Lack of thiamine causes beriberi (I).
Why not the others: Option (B) swaps A and D. Option (C) swaps C and B₁. Option (D) swaps D and C.
Key point: A — eyes, D — bones, C — gums, B₁ — nerves.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Scope, Importance and Breeds
questions.sub_topic: Livestock breeds — which statements are wrong
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Sahiwal is a milch breed of cattle.
(B) Murrah is a well-known buffalo breed of Haryana.
(C) Jamunapari is a breed of sheep.
(D) Kadaknath is an exotic broiler breed developed in the USA.
Which of the statements given above are NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (C) and (D) only
Why: (A) and (B) are true: Sahiwal is a leading milch breed, and Murrah is the best-known buffalo breed, from Haryana. (C) is false: Jamunapari is a goat breed. (D) is false: Kadaknath is an indigenous black-fleshed fowl from Madhya Pradesh.
Why not the others: Options (A) and (C) name true statements as wrong. Option (D) misses statement (C).
Key point: Jamunapari is a goat; Kadaknath is an Indian fowl.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Horticulture: Importance, Orchards, Gardens and Propagation
questions.sub_topic: The quincunx system of orchard layout
questions.question: In the quincunx system of orchard layout:
options: A) plants are set at the corners of equilateral triangles
B) plants are set along the contour lines of a slope
C) rows run east to west with wider spacing between rows
D) an extra plant is set at the centre of each square
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) an extra plant is set at the centre of each square
Why: Quincunx is the square system with one more plant, usually a short-lived filler, at the centre of each square.
Why not the others:
(A) This is the triangular (hexagonal) system.
(B) This is the contour system.
(C) This describes the rectangular system loosely.
Key point: Quincunx = square + a filler in the middle.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Cultivation of Fruits, Vegetables and Flowers
questions.sub_topic: Vegetable that is not a root crop
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a root vegetable?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Potato
Why: The potato is a stem tuber; it bears eyes, which are buds.
Why not the others: (A) radish, (B) carrot and (D) beetroot are swollen roots.
Key point: Potato eyes are buds, which prove it is a stem.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Agrometeorology
questions.sub_topic: Greenhouse gas from flooded paddy fields
questions.question: Flooded rice fields are an important source of which greenhouse gas, linking crop production to climate change?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Methane
Why: In waterlogged soil, oxygen is absent and methanogenic bacteria break down organic matter to release methane.
Why not the others:
(B) Ozone is not produced by paddy soils.
(C) Sulphur dioxide comes mainly from burning fossil fuels.
(D) Chlorofluorocarbons are industrial chemicals.
Key point: Anaerobic paddy soils emit methane.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Soil, Soil Fertility, Fertilizers and Manures
questions.question:
Match List-I (Fertilizer) with List-II (Nutrient content).

List-I
(A) Urea
(B) Diammonium phosphate (DAP)
(C) Muriate of potash (MOP)
(D) Single super phosphate (SSP)

List-II
(I) 46% N
(II) 60% K₂O
(III) 18% N and 46% P₂O₅
(IV) 16% P₂O₅
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (A)-(I), (B)-(III), (C)-(II), (D)-(IV)
Why: Urea has 46% N (I). DAP is 18-46-0 (III). MOP has 60% K₂O (II). SSP has 16% P₂O₅ (IV).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps urea and DAP. Option (C) swaps MOP and SSP. Option (D) swaps DAP and MOP.
Key point: Urea 46 N; DAP 18-46; MOP 60 K₂O; SSP 16 P₂O₅.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Irrigation and Drainage
questions.sub_topic: Index of sodium hazard in irrigation water
questions.question: Which property of irrigation water is used to judge its sodium (sodicity) hazard?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Sodium adsorption ratio (SAR)
Why: SAR compares sodium with calcium and magnesium in water. A high SAR spoils soil structure.
Why not the others:
(B) EC measures salinity, not sodicity.
(C) TDS also reflects total salt content.
(D) BOD measures organic pollution.
Key point: EC tells salinity; SAR tells sodium hazard.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Microbiology
questions.question: In alcoholic fermentation, yeast converts sugar into ethyl alcohol and ________.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) carbon dioxide
Why: Yeast breaks down glucose without oxygen into ethanol and carbon dioxide; the gas is what makes dough rise.
Why not the others:
(A) Fermentation does not release oxygen.
(B) Lactic acid is made by lactic acid bacteria, as in curd.
(C) Methane is made by methanogenic archaea.
Key point: Yeast fermentation: sugar → ethanol + CO₂.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Biochemistry
questions.question: At 25 °C, a neutral solution such as pure water has a pH of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 7
Why: In pure water at 25 °C the concentrations of H⁺ and OH⁻ ions are equal, giving pH 7.
Why not the others:
(A) pH 0 is very strongly acidic.
(B) pH 5 is acidic.
(D) pH 14 is very strongly alkaline.
Key point: Below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral, above 7 is alkaline.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Irrigation and Drainage
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Field capacity is the water a soil holds after excess gravitational water has drained away.
(B) At the permanent wilting point plants wilt and do not recover even in humid air.
(C) Available water is the difference between field capacity and permanent wilting point.
(D) Gravitational water is the main source of water for plants.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (C) only
Why: (A), (B) and (C) are standard definitions. (D) is false: gravitational water drains away quickly; plants rely on capillary water held between field capacity and the wilting point.
Why not the others: Options (B) and (C) include the false statement (D). Option (D) leaves out the true statement (C).
Key point: Available water = field capacity − permanent wilting point.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Biochemistry
questions.question: Sucrose, the sugar extracted from sugarcane, is a disaccharide made of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) glucose and fructose
Why: Sucrose is formed when one glucose unit and one fructose unit join by a glycosidic bond.
Why not the others:
(A) Glucose and galactose form lactose (milk sugar).
(C) Two glucose units form maltose.
(D) Fructose and galactose do not form a common sugar.
Key point: Sucrose = glucose + fructose; lactose = glucose + galactose.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Cultivation of Fruits, Vegetables and Flowers
questions.question: 'Buttoning' in cauliflower, where plants form small, premature curds, is mainly caused by:
options: A) excess irrigation after curd formation
C) boron deficiency in the soil
D) molybdenum deficiency in acid soils
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) transplanting over-aged seedlings
Why: Buttoning is mainly caused by transplanting old seedlings and by nitrogen shortage or other checks to early growth.
Why not the others:
(A) Excess water is not the cause.
(C) Boron deficiency causes browning of the curd.
(D) Molybdenum deficiency causes whiptail.
Key point: Buttoning — old seedlings; browning — boron; whiptail — molybdenum.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Cultivation of Fruits, Vegetables and Flowers
questions.question: Papain, an enzyme used to tenderise meat, is obtained from the latex of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) papaya
Why: Papain is extracted from the latex of unripe papaya fruits.
Why not the others: (B) mango, (C) banana and (D) guava are not sources of papain.
Key point: Papaya latex gives papain.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Scope, Importance and Breeds
questions.question: Which of the following is a draught breed of cattle?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Hallikar
Why: Hallikar of Karnataka is a typical draught breed: strong, fast and hardy, but a poor milker.
Why not the others: (A) Gir, (B) Sahiwal and (D) Red Sindhi are milch breeds.
Key point: Hallikar, Amritmahal and Nagori are draught breeds.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Soil, Soil Fertility, Fertilizers and Manures
questions.sub_topic: Order of soil separates by particle size
questions.question:
Arrange the soil separates from the largest particle size to the smallest.
(A) Silt
(B) Clay
(C) Coarse sand
(D) Fine sand
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (C), (D), (A), (B)
Why: Coarse sand (2.0–0.2 mm) is the largest, then fine sand (0.2–0.02 mm), then silt (0.02–0.002 mm). Clay (below 0.002 mm) is the smallest.
Why not the others: Option (A) puts fine sand first. Option (B) puts silt above fine sand. Option (C) puts clay above silt.
Key point: Sand > silt > clay in particle size.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Care, Management and Diseases
questions.question: Mastitis is the inflammation of the ________ of a milch animal.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) udder
Why: Mastitis is inflammation of the mammary gland (udder), usually from bacterial infection. It lowers milk yield and quality.
Why not the others:
(A) Inflammation of the uterus is metritis.
(B) Rumen disorders include bloat.
(D) Foot rot affects the hoof.
Key point: Mastitis = udder infection; clean milking prevents it.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Seed Science
questions.sub_topic: Order of seed classes in production
questions.question:
Arrange the classes of seed in the order in which they are produced in the seed chain.
(A) Breeder seed
(B) Certified seed
(C) Foundation seed
(D) Nucleus seed
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (D), (A), (C), (B)
Why: The breeder keeps a small stock of nucleus seed (D). It is multiplied into breeder seed (A). Breeder seed is multiplied into foundation seed (C). Foundation seed is multiplied into certified seed (B) for farmers.
Why not the others: Option (A) puts foundation before breeder seed. Option (B) starts with breeder seed. Option (D) puts certified seed before foundation seed.
Key point: Nucleus → breeder → foundation → certified.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Irrigation and Drainage
questions.sub_topic: Most critical irrigation stage of wheat
questions.question: For wheat, the single most critical stage for irrigation is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) crown root initiation
Why: Crown root initiation (CRI), about 20–25 days after sowing, is the most critical stage. Stress then sharply cuts tillers and yield.
Why not the others: (A) tillering, (B) jointing and (C) dough are also irrigation stages, but none is as critical as CRI.
Key point: If only one irrigation is possible in wheat, give it at CRI.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Care, Management and Diseases
questions.question:
Match List-I (Disease) with List-II (Causal organism).

List-I
(A) Coccidiosis
(B) Black quarter
(C) Haemorrhagic septicaemia
(D) Ranikhet disease

List-II
(I) *Pasteurella multocida*
(II) Avian paramyxovirus (Newcastle disease virus)
(III) *Clostridium chauvoei*
(IV) *Eimeria* species
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A)-(IV), (B)-(III), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Coccidiosis is caused by protozoa of the genus *Eimeria* (IV). Black quarter is caused by the bacterium *Clostridium chauvoei* (III). Haemorrhagic septicaemia is caused by *Pasteurella multocida* (I). Ranikhet disease is caused by a paramyxovirus (II).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps coccidiosis and black quarter. Option (B) swaps black quarter and HS. Option (C) swaps HS and Ranikhet.
Key point: Protozoan, two bacteria and a virus: know which is which.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Agrometeorology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements about the Indian monsoon:
(A) The southwest monsoon normally sets in over Kerala around 1 June.
(B) The northeast monsoon brings rain to coastal Tamil Nadu in October to December.
(C) A 'break in the monsoon' means that the monsoon has withdrawn for the season.
(D) El Niño years are often linked with weak monsoon rainfall in India.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: (A) is true: the normal onset date over Kerala is about 1 June. (B) is true: the retreating (northeast) monsoon gives Tamil Nadu its main rainy season. (C) is false: a break is a dry spell of some days or weeks within the monsoon, after which rain returns. (D) is true: El Niño (warm Pacific waters) is often associated with deficient Indian monsoons.
Why not the others: Options (A), (B) and (C) all include statement (C), which is false.
Key point: A break is a pause inside the monsoon, not its end.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.sub_topic: Order of the stages of mitosis
questions.question:
Arrange the stages of mitosis in the order in which they occur.
(A) Anaphase
(B) Prophase
(C) Telophase
(D) Metaphase
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B), (D), (A), (C)
Why: In prophase (B) the chromosomes condense. In metaphase (D) they line up at the equator. In anaphase (A) the sister chromatids separate to the poles. In telophase (C) new nuclei form.
Why not the others: Option (A) puts anaphase before metaphase. Option (C) starts with metaphase. Option (D) puts telophase before anaphase.
Key point: The order is prophase, metaphase, anaphase, telophase (PMAT).

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Crop Production: Introduction and Modern Agriculture
questions.sub_topic: Crop that is not a pulse
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a pulse crop?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Sesame
Why: Sesame (til) is an oilseed crop.
Why not the others: (A) pigeon pea, (B) chickpea and (C) black gram are pulses.
Key point: Pulses are edible legume seeds; sesame belongs with the oilseeds.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Horticulture: Importance, Orchards, Gardens and Propagation
questions.sub_topic: Plant that completes its life in one season
questions.question: A plant that completes its life cycle, from seed to seed, within one season is called:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) an annual
Why: Annuals such as marigold complete their life cycle in a single season.
Why not the others:
(A) Perennials live for many years.
(C) Biennials need two seasons.
(D) A shrub is a woody plant of a certain form, not a life-span class.
Key point: Annual — one season; biennial — two; perennial — many years.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Scope, Importance and Breeds
questions.question: Who is known as the Father of the White Revolution in India?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Verghese Kurien
Why: Verghese Kurien led the National Dairy Development Board and Operation Flood, which made India the world's largest milk producer.
Why not the others:
(A) Swaminathan is linked with the Green Revolution in India.
(B) Borlaug developed the semi-dwarf wheats of the Green Revolution.
(C) Subramaniam was the agriculture minister during the Green Revolution.
Key point: White Revolution = milk = Kurien.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.sub_topic: Not a method of crop breeding
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a method of breeding crop varieties?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Vernalization
Why: Vernalization is a cold treatment that hastens flowering; it does not create or select a new variety.
Why not the others: (B) introduction, (C) hybridization and (D) mutation breeding are all standard methods of crop improvement.
Key point: Breeding methods change or select the genetic make-up; vernalization does not.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Horticulture: Importance, Orchards, Gardens and Propagation
questions.sub_topic: Fruit crops and their common propagation methods
questions.question:
Match List-I (Fruit crop) with List-II (Common method of propagation).

List-I
(A) Mango
(B) Banana
(C) Guava
(D) Grape

List-II
(I) Hardwood cuttings
(II) Suckers
(III) Air layering
(IV) Softwood or veneer grafting
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(IV), (B)-(II), (C)-(III), (D)-(I)
Why: Mango is grafted, often by softwood or veneer grafting (IV). Banana is grown from suckers (II). Guava is commonly multiplied by air layering (III). Grape is raised from hardwood cuttings (I).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps mango and banana. Option (B) swaps guava and grape. Option (D) swaps mango and guava.
Key point: Each fruit has its preferred method: graft mango, sucker banana, layer guava, cut grape.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Care, Management and Diseases
questions.sub_topic: Why a newborn calf needs colostrum early
questions.question: Why should a newborn calf be fed colostrum within the first hours of birth?
options: A) Because colostrum is low in protein and easy to digest
B) Because it gives the calf antibodies that protect it from disease
C) Because it makes the calf gain weight faster than whole milk does
D) Because it removes the need for vaccination later
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Because it gives the calf antibodies that protect it from disease
Why: Colostrum is rich in immunoglobulins (antibodies). The calf's gut can absorb them intact only in the first hours of life, which gives it passive immunity.
Why not the others:
(A) Colostrum is high in protein, not low.
(C) Its key value is immunity, not faster weight gain.
(D) Calves still need vaccination later.
Key point: Colostrum first, and fast: it carries the mother's antibodies.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Livestock: Care, Management and Diseases
questions.question: A balanced ration for a farm animal is best defined as feed that:
options: A) supplies all nutrients in the right amounts and proportions for 24 hours
B) contains equal weights of green fodder and dry fodder every day
C) is made only of concentrates such as oilcakes, bran and grain
D) is given in two equal meals, morning and evening, every day
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) supplies all nutrients in the right amounts and proportions for 24 hours
Why: A balanced ration provides all the nutrients an animal needs, in the correct amount and proportion, over a 24-hour period.
Why not the others:
(B) Equal weights of green and dry fodder do not guarantee balance.
(C) Concentrates alone are not a balanced ration for ruminants.
(D) The number of meals does not define a balanced ration.
Key point: Balanced = right nutrients, right proportion, for a full day.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Soil, Soil Fertility, Fertilizers and Manures
questions.sub_topic: Urea needed for a given nitrogen dose
questions.question: A farmer needs to apply 92 kg of nitrogen per hectare using urea alone. How much urea is required?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 200 kg
Why: Step 1: urea contains 46% N, so 100 kg urea gives 46 kg N.
Step 2: urea needed = 92 × 100 ÷ 46.
Step 3: 9200 ÷ 46 = 200 kg.
Why not the others:
(A) 100 kg gives only 46 kg N.
(B) 150 kg gives 69 kg N.
(D) 250 kg gives 115 kg N.
Key point: Fertilizer needed = nutrient dose × 100 ÷ % nutrient.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Artificial Insemination and Livestock Products
questions.question:
Arrange the steps of artificial insemination in the correct order.
(A) Dilution of semen with an extender
(B) Collection of semen with an artificial vagina
(C) Insemination of a cow in heat
(D) Storage of frozen semen in liquid nitrogen
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (B), (A), (D), (C)
Why: Semen is first collected from the bull with an artificial vagina (B). It is then diluted with an extender (A). It is frozen and stored in liquid nitrogen at −196 °C (D). Finally, it is deposited in a cow that is in heat (C).
Why not the others: Option (B) dilutes before collecting. Option (C) stores the semen before diluting it. Option (D) inseminates before storage.
Key point: Collect → dilute → freeze and store → inseminate.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Soil, Soil Fertility, Fertilizers and Manures
questions.sub_topic: Nutrient behind khaira disease of rice
questions.question: 'Khaira' disease of rice, with rusty-brown patches on the leaves, is caused by a deficiency of:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) zinc
Why: Khaira is a zinc deficiency disorder, common in alkaline, calcareous and waterlogged soils. It is corrected by zinc sulphate.
Why not the others:
(A) Iron deficiency causes interveinal chlorosis of young leaves.
(C) Boron deficiency affects growing points and grain set.
(D) Manganese deficiency causes grey speck in oats and chlorosis.
Key point: Khaira of rice = zinc deficiency; remedy zinc sulphate.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Agrometeorology
questions.question: Which instrument is used to measure the relative humidity of the air?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) Hygrometer
Why: A hygrometer (for example, a wet-and-dry-bulb psychrometer) measures atmospheric humidity.
Why not the others:
(A) An anemometer measures wind speed.
(C) A barometer measures air pressure.
(D) A rain gauge measures rainfall.
Key point: Hygro- means moisture: the hygrometer measures humidity.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Fruit and Vegetable Preservation
questions.question: Which constituent of fruit is chiefly responsible for the setting of jelly?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Pectin
Why: Pectin, with the right amounts of sugar and acid, forms the gel that makes jelly set.
Why not the others:
(A) Starch makes jelly cloudy.
(B) Cellulose does not dissolve or form a gel.
(C) Tannin gives astringency, not setting.
Key point: Jelly needs pectin, acid and sugar in balance.

questions.topic: Unit 4 (Horticulture): Fruit and Vegetable Preservation
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Sugar in high concentration preserves food by drawing water out of microbes.
(B) Potassium metabisulphite is the preferred preservative for coloured juices such as jamun.
(C) Low temperature slows the growth of microbes and the activity of enzymes.
(D) Fruit juices are usually pasteurised below 100 °C.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) (B) only
Why: (B) is false: potassium metabisulphite releases sulphur dioxide, which bleaches the natural colour (anthocyanins) of fruits such as jamun. Sodium benzoate is used for coloured juices. (A), (C) and (D) are true.
Why not the others: Statements (A), (C) and (D) are all correct.
Key point: KMS for light-coloured products; sodium benzoate for coloured ones.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Crop Production: Introduction and Modern Agriculture
questions.sub_topic: Modern agriculture — which statement is wrong
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Conservation agriculture rests on minimum soil disturbance, permanent soil cover and crop rotation.
(B) Precision agriculture uses GPS and variable-rate application to match inputs to differences within a field.
(C) Organic farming allows small doses of synthetic urea to correct nitrogen deficiency.
(D) Remote sensing can judge crop health using vegetation indices such as NDVI.
Which of the statements given above is NOT correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (C) only
Why: (C) is false: organic farming does not allow synthetic fertilizers such as urea. Nitrogen comes from manures, legumes and biofertilizers. (A), (B) and (D) are correct descriptions.
Why not the others: Statements (A), (B) and (D) are all true.
Key point: Organic farming excludes synthetic fertilizers and pesticides.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Weed Control
questions.question: Which of the following herbicides is non-selective, killing almost all green plants it touches?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Glyphosate
Why: Glyphosate is a broad-spectrum, non-selective, systemic herbicide.
Why not the others:
(A) 2,4-D is selective against broad-leaved weeds.
(B) Atrazine is selective in maize and sorghum.
(D) Pendimethalin is a selective pre-emergence herbicide.
Key point: Glyphosate kills almost everything green; use it on non-crop land or before sowing.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Artificial Insemination and Livestock Products
questions.sub_topic: Time and temperature of HTST pasteurisation
questions.question: In the HTST (high temperature, short time) method, milk is pasteurised at:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) 72 °C for 15 seconds
Why: HTST pasteurisation heats milk to at least 72 °C for 15 seconds and then cools it quickly.
Why not the others:
(A) 63 °C for 30 minutes is the LTLT (holder) method.
(C) 135 °C for about 2 seconds is UHT treatment.
(D) Boiling for 10 minutes is not a pasteurisation standard.
Key point: LTLT 63 °C/30 min; HTST 72 °C/15 s; UHT about 135 °C/2 s.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Crop Production: Introduction and Modern Agriculture
questions.question: Berseem (Egyptian clover) is grown mainly as a ________ crop.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) forage
Why: Berseem is a leguminous fodder crop of the rabi season, cut several times for green feed.
Why not the others:
(B) Fibre crops include cotton and jute.
(C) Oilseeds include mustard and groundnut.
(D) Sugar crops include sugarcane and sugar beet.
Key point: Berseem is the "king of fodders" in rabi.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Microbiology
questions.question:
Consider the following statements:
(A) Bacteria are prokaryotes and have no membrane-bound nucleus.
(B) Actinomycetes produce the earthy smell of freshly ploughed moist soil.
(C) Viruses can multiply on dead organic matter outside living cells.
(D) Fungi are the main decomposers in acidic soils.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A), (B) and (D) only
Why: (A) is true: bacterial DNA lies free in the cytoplasm. (B) is true: actinomycetes release geosmin, which gives wet soil its smell. (C) is false: viruses multiply only inside living host cells. (D) is true: fungi tolerate low pH better than bacteria and dominate decomposition in acid soils.
Why not the others: Options (B) and (C) include the false statement (C). Option (D) leaves out the true statement (D).
Key point: Viruses are obligate parasites; they cannot multiply outside living cells.

questions.topic: Unit 2 (Livestock Production): Fisheries
questions.question: Which of the following is an Indian major carp?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Rohu
Why: The Indian major carps are catla, rohu and mrigal.
Why not the others: (A) grass carp, (B) silver carp and (D) common carp are exotic carps brought into India.
Key point: Indian major carps: catla, rohu and mrigal.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Weed Control
questions.sub_topic: Weeds and the crops they infest
questions.question:
Match List-I (Weed) with List-II (Crop it chiefly infests).

List-I
(A) *Phalaris minor*
(B) *Orobanche* (broomrape)
(C) *Echinochloa crus-galli*
(D) *Cuscuta* (dodder)

List-II
(I) Mustard
(II) Berseem and lucerne
(III) Wheat
(IV) Rice
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) (A)-(III), (B)-(I), (C)-(IV), (D)-(II)
Why: *Phalaris minor* is the main grass weed of wheat (III). Broomrape is a root parasite of mustard (I). Barnyard grass infests rice (IV). Dodder is a stem parasite of berseem and lucerne (II).
Why not the others: Option (B) swaps *Phalaris* and *Echinochloa*. Option (C) swaps broomrape and dodder. Option (D) swaps *Phalaris* and broomrape.
Key point: Phalaris–wheat, Orobanche–mustard, Echinochloa–rice, Cuscuta–berseem.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.question: Why did the seven pairs of traits Mendel studied in pea assort independently, with no sign of linkage?
options: A) Because pea is a cross-pollinated plant with many wild relatives
B) Because he studied only one generation of each of his crosses
C) Because all seven genes lay close together on a single chromosome
D) Because the genes lay on different chromosomes or far apart on the same one
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Because the genes lay on different chromosomes or far apart on the same one
Why: Genes that sit on different chromosomes, or far apart on one chromosome, are inherited independently, so Mendel saw no linkage.
Why not the others:
(A) Pea is normally self-pollinated, which helped Mendel.
(B) He followed the F₁ and F₂ generations and beyond.
(C) Genes close together on one chromosome would show linkage.
Key point: Independent assortment holds for unlinked genes.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Microbiology
questions.question: Which group of microorganisms is photosynthetic, fixes atmospheric nitrogen and is used as a biofertilizer in flooded rice fields?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) Blue-green algae (cyanobacteria)
Why: Blue-green algae such as *Anabaena* and *Nostoc* photosynthesise and fix nitrogen in their heterocysts, and they thrive in standing water.
Why not the others:
(A) Actinomycetes are mainly decomposers.
(B) Protozoa feed on bacteria and do not fix nitrogen.
(C) Yeasts are fungi and do not fix nitrogen.
Key point: Cyanobacteria are the classic biofertilizer of wetland rice.

questions.topic: Unit 1 (Agrometeorology, Genetics and Plant Breeding, Biochemistry and Microbiology): Genetics and Plant Breeding
questions.question:
Match List-I (Organelle) with List-II (Main function).

List-I
(A) Mitochondrion
(B) Ribosome
(C) Chloroplast
(D) Golgi apparatus

List-II
(I) Photosynthesis
(II) Packaging and secretion of materials
(III) Aerobic respiration and ATP production
(IV) Protein synthesis
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) (A)-(III), (B)-(IV), (C)-(I), (D)-(II)
Why: Mitochondria carry out aerobic respiration and make ATP (III). Ribosomes are the site of protein synthesis (IV). Chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis (I). The Golgi apparatus packages and secretes materials (II).
Why not the others: Option (A) swaps mitochondria and ribosomes. Option (B) swaps chloroplast and Golgi. Option (D) swaps mitochondria and chloroplast.
Key point: Mitochondria make energy; chloroplasts trap it.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Field Crops: Cultivation, Protection and Post-harvest
questions.sub_topic: Purpose of puddling a rice field
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Rice is the staple food of more than half of India's people, and most of it is grown in the kharif season. In irrigated areas the crop is usually raised first in a nursery. When the seedlings are about three to four weeks old, they are pulled out and transplanted into puddled fields. Puddling means ploughing the field while it is under standing water. It breaks down the soil structure, cuts the loss of water by deep percolation and buries many weeds. Two or three seedlings are planted on each hill at a spacing of about 20 cm × 15 cm. A shallow layer of water, about 5 cm deep, is kept in the field for most of the season, because rice tolerates flooding and standing water keeps weeds down. The crop suffers most from water stress at panicle initiation and at flowering. Too much nitrogen makes the plants soft and leafy, so they lodge easily and attract the brown planthopper, an insect that sucks sap at the base of the plants and causes patches of dried crop called 'hopper burn'. In the System of Rice Intensification (SRI), farmers transplant single young seedlings only 8 to 12 days old at a wider spacing of 25 cm × 25 cm and keep the soil moist but not flooded, which saves a great deal of water. The crop is harvested when about four-fifths of the grains in the panicle have turned straw-coloured.

Question: According to the passage, puddling a rice field helps mainly because it:
options: A) adds nitrogen to the soil from the standing water
B) reduces the loss of water by deep percolation
C) raises the soil temperature for faster germination
D) loosens the soil so that roots go deeper
questions.explanation:
Answer: (B) reduces the loss of water by deep percolation
Why: The passage says puddling breaks down soil structure, cuts the loss of water by deep percolation and buries weeds.
Why not the others:
(A) Standing water does not add nitrogen; the passage says nothing of the kind.
(C) Soil temperature is not mentioned.
(D) Puddling compacts and smears the soil rather than loosening it for deep roots.
Key point: Puddling seals the soil so that water stands in the field.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Field Crops: Cultivation, Protection and Post-harvest
questions.sub_topic: Age of seedlings in SRI as described
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

The crop is harvested when about four-fifths of the grains in the panicle have turned straw-coloured.

Question: In the System of Rice Intensification described in the passage, the seedlings transplanted are:
options: A) three to four weeks old, two or three per hill
B) about six weeks old, planted close together
C) 8 to 12 days old, one per hill
D) sown directly without any nursery
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) 8 to 12 days old, one per hill
Why: The passage says SRI uses single young seedlings only 8 to 12 days old at a wider spacing.
Why not the others:
(A) This describes the usual transplanted crop, not SRI.
(B) Six-week-old seedlings are not mentioned, and SRI uses wide spacing.
(D) SRI in the passage is a transplanting method.
Key point: SRI means young, single seedlings, wide spacing and moist (not flooded) soil.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Field Crops: Cultivation, Protection and Post-harvest
questions.sub_topic: Insect linked to excess nitrogen in the passage
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

The crop is harvested when about four-fifths of the grains in the panicle have turned straw-coloured.

Question: Which insect does the passage link with heavy nitrogen use and 'hopper burn'?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (A) Brown planthopper
Why: The passage says too much nitrogen attracts the brown planthopper, which sucks sap at the base of the plants and causes hopper burn.
Why not the others:
(B), (C) and (D) are real rice pests, but the passage does not mention them, and none of them causes hopper burn.
Key point: Brown planthopper sucks sap at the plant base; heavy nitrogen favours it.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Field Crops: Cultivation, Protection and Post-harvest
questions.sub_topic: Hills per square metre at the stated spacing
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Rice is the staple food of more than half of India's people, and most of it is grown in the kharif season. In irrigated areas the crop is usually raised first in a nursery. When the seedlings are about three to four weeks old, they are pulled out and transplanted into puddled fields. Puddling means ploughing the field while it is under standing water. It breaks down the soil structure, cuts the loss of water by deep percolation and buries many weeds. Two or three seedlings are planted on each hill at a spacing of about 20 cm × 15 cm. A shallow layer of water, about 5 cm deep, is kept in the field for most of the season, because rice tolerates flooding and standing water keeps weeds down. The crop suffers most from water stress at panicle initiation and at flowering. Too much nitrogen makes the plants soft and leafy, so they lodge easily and attract the brown planthopper, an insect that sucks sap at the base of the plants and causes patches of dried crop called 'hopper burn'. In the System of Rice Intensification (SRI), farmers transplant single young seedlings only 8 to 12 days old at a wider spacing of 25 cm × 25 cm and keep the soil moist but not flooded, which saves a great deal of water. The crop is harvested when about four-fifths of the grains in the panicle have turned straw-coloured.

Question: Using the normal transplanting spacing given in the passage, about how many hills are there in one square metre?
questions.explanation:
Answer: (D) 33
Why: Step 1: one square metre = 100 cm × 100 cm = 10,000 cm².
Step 2: area per hill = 20 cm × 15 cm = 300 cm².
Step 3: hills per m² = 10,000 ÷ 300 ≈ 33.
Why not the others:
(A) 15 and (B) 20 come from using a single side of the spacing.
(C) 25 would need 400 cm² per hill (20 cm × 20 cm).
Key point: Plant population = area ÷ area per plant.

questions.topic: Unit 3 (Crop Production): Field Crops: Cultivation, Protection and Post-harvest
questions.sub_topic: What the passage implies about saving water in rice
questions.question:
Read the following passage and answer the question that follows.

Rice is the staple food of more than half of India's people, and most of it is grown in the kharif season. In irrigated areas the crop is usually raised first in a nursery. When the seedlings are about three to four weeks old, they are pulled out and transplanted into puddled fields. Puddling means ploughing the field while it is under standing water. It breaks down the soil structure, cuts the loss of water by deep percolation and buries many weeds. Two or three seedlings are planted on each hill at a spacing of about 20 cm × 15 cm. A shallow layer of water, about 5 cm deep, is kept in the field for most of the season, because rice tolerates flooding and standing water keeps weeds down. The crop suffers most from water stress at panicle initiation and at flowering. Too much nitrogen makes the plants soft and leafy, so they lodge easily and attract the brown planthopper, an insect that sucks sap at the base of the plants and causes patches of dried crop called 'hopper burn'. In the System of Rice Intensification (SRI), farmers transplant single young seedlings only 8 to 12 days old at a wider spacing of 25 cm × 25 cm and keep the soil moist but not flooded, which saves a great deal of water. The crop is harvested when about four-fifths of the grains in the panicle have turned straw-coloured.

Question: Which conclusion is best supported by the passage?
options: A) Rice must always be kept under deep water to give a good yield.
B) Water stress matters least at flowering, so irrigation can stop then.
C) Rice can be grown with less water if the soil is kept moist rather than flooded.
D) Wider spacing in SRI is used mainly to increase the brown planthopper.
questions.explanation:
Answer: (C) Rice can be grown with less water if the soil is kept moist rather than flooded.
Why: The passage says that SRI keeps the soil moist but not flooded and saves a great deal of water.
Why not the others:
(A) The passage calls for a shallow layer of about 5 cm, and SRI avoids flooding altogether.
(B) The passage says flowering is one of the most sensitive stages.
(D) This is the reverse of the passage, which links the planthopper to excess nitrogen.
Key point: Rice needs moisture, not necessarily standing water.
